subject.title: Node host: no SSH transport support + challenge auth fails behind reverse proxy

question: Should `openclaw node run` gain first-class managed SSH transport and remote-token pairing behavior, or should OpenClaw keep manual SSH tunnels as the supported node-host path while improving diagnostics and docs?
rationale: This choice changes how remote node hosts authenticate, how SSH tunnels are supervised by services, and whether a tunneled remote node is treated as local or remote for device and node pairing policy.

options.title: Define remote node-host contract
options.body: Keep this issue open, coordinate the auth and approval overlap with https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/91126, and require live reverse-proxy or managed-tunnel proof before closing.

options.title: Split transport from auth policy
options.body: Track managed SSH separately and narrow this issue to reverse-proxy pairing/auth only after current-main live reproduction is available.

options.title: Keep manual SSH as supported path
options.body: Close only after maintainers explicitly decide not to manage node-host SSH in core and update docs or diagnostics to steer users to manual tunnels.

recommendation.title: Define remote node-host contract
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open, coordinate the auth and approval overlap with https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/91126, and require live reverse-proxy or managed-tunnel proof before closing.

likelyOwner.reason: This account is the strongest current-history owner for the node-host runner, SSH helper, node CLI, and gateway-client handshake boundaries involved in the decision.
